verdict: Approve with changes. The ownership model is sound and fits the lesson's scope: the records Application owns records, selection, loading and results; Views render and emit intent; Regions handle placement; the workspace Application exists only to own an optional lifetime. Startup and teardown are correct within scope. Before merge, the broad catch in loadRecords needs narrowing because it teaches agents to hide render bugs, and the documented open-failure path needs a test. The request guard repeats itself and can be reduced to one check. Based only on the supplied diff; nothing was run.
blockingIssues: loadRecords' try is too wide: it wraps clearRecords(), records.reset() and the state update, so any exception during row render shows as 'Could not load records.' Agents copy the pattern, so the example teaches that render bugs look like network errors. Put only the await service.list(...) call inside the try.

Open failure is documented but not tested: architecture.md says that if opening fails, the workspace stops the child and shows an error. WorkspaceApplication.openRecords does this with no test and no logging. Either test it or remove the claim, and log the caught error so it isn't silently lost.
risks: Stale detail after an in-run reload: loadRecords leaves selectedId alone while clearRecords destroys the old Models, so with a selection, reloading on a ready screen keeps DetailView bound to a destroyed Model. The UI can't trigger this yet (Retry only appears on error), but the supersession tests call it directly and the later refresh lesson will run into it.

clearRecords depends on @mnjs/data Model.destroy() semantics. If it behaves like Backbone (remove from collection, sync or delete events), the example will copy and spread that behaviour. Confirm it is purely local.

The same-run supersession tests call feature.loadRecords() directly and swap feature.options.service, which locks in a private method and a mutable options contract. No UI path makes two loads in one run in this lesson, and peer-comparison.md defers supersession coverage to the refresh lesson, so the tests contradict the plan.
releaseRun's stopListening on the status/list children may repeat cleanup the framework already does on View destroy. If so, it is extra noise for readers to copy. Verify before keeping it.

records.md links examples/records/README.md and runs examples/records/playwright.config.js; main.js imports styles.css; records-api.js fetches /api/records.json. None are in the changed-file list, so confirm they are committed. The 30 passing runs suggest the config exists; the README link is unconfirmed.
Evidence item 5 (deliberate-defect checks) is still pending. Don't describe the suite as sensitive or regression-proof until it is done.
The Clear-selection extension is unaccepted subagent work. Keep it out of this merge unless its parent acceptance test lands with it.
incorrectAssumptions: The five isCurrent conditions are not independent. releaseRun aborts the request, root View loss calls releaseRun, and a new load aborts the previous request, so request.signal.aborted alone is enough, even when the service ignores cancellation, because the check is on our own controller.

The lesson says 'Retry uses the same loadRecords operation' and the tests treat loadRecords as safe to call at any time. Safe any-time reload is a refresh behaviour, which the lesson has deferred, and it isn't consistent here: selection survives while the Models it points to are destroyed.

The final teardown test only shows that onBeforeDestroy works. It does not cover state disposal from a feature that was never started, so a general 'createState is owned/disposed' claim is unchecked on that path.
missingTests: Open fails (make records.start reject): the child is stopped, 'Could not open records.' shows in the surviving shell, and the next Open works.
Clicking Open twice (or Open while already open) makes exactly one request and one mounted feature. This tests the idempotent start behaviour the workspace relies on.
Close in the error state, then reopen: Retry is gone and a fresh load starts.
A row render that throws after a successful fetch is not reported as a load error (regression guard for the try-narrowing fix).

The pending deliberate-defect checks: remove the abort check, skip releaseRun in onBeforeStop, drop the explicit showDetail() in onBeforeStart, and drop clearRecords in onBeforeDestroy. Each should fail the matching test for the expected reason.
simplifications: Replace isCurrent() with a single 'if (request.signal.aborted) return false;' after the await and in the catch. Shorten the guard list in architecture.md to: abort is the invalidation; check it before applying a result or error.
Narrow the try to the service call: let records; try { records = await service.list(...) } catch { set error status; return false; }, then apply the result outside the try.

Either drop the two same-run supersession tests (the reopen-after-close stale test already covers a service that ignores cancellation), or keep them and clear selectedId / call showDetail on a successful reload so reload is actually safe.
Remove the child stopListening loop in releaseRun if View destroy already cleans up inbound listeners.
nextSteps: Narrow the try and reduce the guard to signal.aborted; update records.md and architecture.md to match.
Add the open-failure and double-Open tests; log the caught open error.
Choose one: drop the same-run supersession tests, or clear selection on reload. Record the choice.
Run the deliberate-defect checks and record which test fails for each defect.
Confirm the README, playwright.config.js, styles.css and api/records.json are committed and the links resolve.
Keep the Clear-selection extension out until its parent acceptance test passes.
